How do the dev’s work, earnings, and sales affect buyers?

Two sides, one changing market

The dev may launch, promote, build, earn fees, sell tokens, reinvest, or leave. Buyers may discover, investigate, buy, hold, add, or sell. These actions can happen in different orders and repeat.

Useful work and credible promotion can bring buyers. Trading can generate fees that fund more work. But the dev may earn from volume while buyers depend on price and enough liquidity to sell. Record both sides to see whether their interests continue to line up.

The interaction layer

What you observeDev questionBuyer question
Work and promotionWhat was delivered or paid for?Is there a current reason to buy?
InventoryWhat was sold, transferred, or unlocked?How much could still reach the market?
Volume and feesWho earns, and how much?Who is trading and what are the costs?
LiquidityWho can withdraw or change it?What does a size-specific sale quote show?
Repeat participationDoes the work bring returning users?Do buyers keep coming after promotion stops?

How to investigate it

Keep a dated table with creator actions, buyer activity, sources, and unresolved questions. Use the same time windows and pool coverage. A release followed by buying is worth investigating, but timing alone does not tell you the release caused the buying.

Check what changes when fees fall, a release is delayed, a competing token attracts buyers, or the group sells more. Write the next observation that would change your view.

Practical case — illustrative

At 11:00 UTC, SAMPLE's dev delivers a promised update. Group available holdings are 8m after Section 9. Other observed buying picked up briefly, then slowed. The creator received fee income while the market was active.

Record the delivered update and fee claim. Continuing buyer interest still needs checking. If returning users and independent buying persist across comparable windows, add those observations to the record rather than assuming the update was enough.

Keep this record

Save a creator/buyer timeline: date/time, verified action, group holdings/earnings, buyer activity, depth, sources, and what to check next. Use Section 9 to review sales and spending.

Add these findings to your review worksheet →

Check your understanding — answered

The dev is working. Should buyers keep holding? Recheck the reason for buying, available supply, and trading conditions.

Buyers are excited. Are interests aligned? Review control rights, earnings, delivery, and sales.

Does a productive relationship require constant price rises? Check work and participation over time; short-term price moves do not settle that question.

SAMPLE is made up for this course. Date each finding. For a real token, use current transaction records and platform rules. Inspect shows sampled trades; use external records to check ownership and permissions.
